rulings.decision: THE RUNNER IS WRONG. If the runner stops a run itself before Ready because it lost the control check, the FINAL must be outer errorCode RUN_ERROR with errorMessage = the launcher's fixed reason, which is 'CANCELLED' on abort. Every source step must be SKIPPED with null timings and browserStartedAt null. This is the shape the drain path already sends. Outer CANCELLED is kept only when a backend-recorded fact backs the stop: DELETE relay, or a progress-ack/control-ack with cancelRequested or revoked true. The backend stays unchanged.
why: Contract meaning: outer CANCELLED is the runner's answer to a recorded cancel (openapi runnerCancelRun; errors.ts CANCELLED doc 'the API assigns its own CANCELLED only where it recorded the request'). A control-window loss is not a cancel anyone requested. Labelling it CANCELLED would invent a cause, which OBS-007 AC-13 forbids ('control-network loss stay unmapped').

Fail-closed: the backend pre-Ready edge (ADMITTED->FINALIZING with no STARTED) is the narrow OBS-006 exception, security-reviewed and pinned by AdmissionCasIT L453-456. Accepting outer CANCELLED there without cancel_requested_at would broaden a reviewed ledger edge. It would need a new security review. It contradicts design §2 'does not replace/broaden that path'.

No new code is needed. RUN_ERROR is an existing runner code, and 'CANCELLED' is already in the backend's fixed pre-Ready reason set. Nothing changes in the one-vocabulary set (Java enum / OpenAPI / V13 CHECK), the contracts or the migrations. The API result is ERROR with error_code NULL and the reason in the bounded diagnostic, which is exactly the 'unmapped cancellation' AC-13 prescribes.

rejectedAlternative.option: Backend accepts outer CANCELLED on the pre-Ready branch without a recorded cancel
rejectedAlternative.rejectedBecause: It broadens a security-reviewed fail-closed predicate. It contradicts the OpenAPI meaning of CANCELLED and design §2. It breaks the existing AdmissionCasIT pin. It hides a runner misclassification instead of fixing it. The API outcome would be the same (error_code null), so it buys nothing.

rulings.acceptedEdge: Race: the user's cancel is recorded after the runner already self-stopped, and the upgrade window has passed. The backend then sees cancelled=true and takes the normal applyFinal path (ADMITTED+cancel_requested_at is admitted). The row ends ERROR with error_code NULL instead of CANCELLED. Accepted: the runner did not stop because of the user's request, and adding a backend RUN_ERROR->CANCELLED mapping would broaden the contract's two mappings. Rejected.

rulings.topic: Logging the rejection; retry vs settle

decision.logging: YES, IN 012A, two lines, both fixed text. (a) ChecksExceptionHandler.handleInternalCallback logs WARN 'Studio internal callback refused: status={} code={}' with the HTTP status and the InternalCallbackCodes constant only. Never log ex.getMessage(): several messages interpolate runner-supplied strings. (b) ProgressReportService, at the observedPreReady branch, logs WARN once with pathExecutionId and a server-side category enum for the failed clause of requireObservedPreReadyFailure (KIND | ORIGIN | RESULT | OUTER_CODE | REASON | COORDINATES | LOG_READING). Nothing from the report (no errorMessage, no codes as received, no body) goes into the log. The HTTP response body stays exactly as today (data-free INVALID_REPORT, same message), so there is no contract change.
decision.retry: NO retry. A 400 is a deterministic refusal of byte-identical bytes, and reportClient's non-retryable classification of 400 is correct and stays. The fix is to send a valid FINAL the first time (R8.1).
decision.settle: NO settle-on-reject. A rejected report must apply nothing (fail-closed; 'a silent coercion is a divergence nobody ever finds'). The existing RunningReaper backstop (manifest reconcile, else START_TIMEOUT, or CANCELLED if recorded) is the settlement and stays unchanged. No timeout, TTL or deadline change.
decision.deferred: To STUDIO-OBS-009 (deployable single path / live proof): an operational alert on the runner counter terminalAbandoned / report.terminal_rejected, and a live check that a rejected terminal is settled by the reaper within start_deadline + one recovery poll. Neither is a 012A requirement.

rulings.why: The cost of (a) and (b) is two log statements and one enum. Without them, the next mismatch of this class (see ADJ-1, ADJ-2) is again diagnosable only by reading code. Security: fixed templates, server-owned identifiers and constants only, so there is no log injection and no canary path.

adjacentFindings.status: found by code reading; not executed; not in R8 scope
adjacentFindings.what: Revocation recorded while the row is still ADMITTED (pre-Ready) with no cancel_requested_at. ProgressReportService excludes revoked rows from the observedPreReady branch, and the normal applyFinal admits ADMITTED only with cancel_requested_at, so the runner's recorded-revocation FINAL (outer CANCELLED) gets 0 rows, then a 409 refusal, then OWNERSHIP_LOST. The row settles only via the reaper as ERROR with error_code NULL (reconcile) or START_TIMEOUT, never AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED. The OpenAPI AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED row covers dispatcher denial before send and live revocation after start, but not this window.
adjacentFindings.disposition: Root/@po decide. Recommended home: STUDIO-OBS-009, starting with a failing probe IT. R8's runner change does not alter this path.

adjacentFindings.status: found by code reading; not executed; not in R8 scope
adjacentFindings.what: launcher.ts L485 emits 'LAUNCH_UNKNOWN' when there is no child result and no abort (pinned by deadline-outcome.test.ts row 2 against a permissive fake). 'LAUNCH_UNKNOWN' is not in the backend pre-Ready reason set, so that FINAL is also refused with 400 and the row waits for the reaper (START_TIMEOUT). The OBS-006 design §2 lists only the child IPC reasons; it explicitly leaves BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED/START_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED parent residuals unadmitted but does not name LAUNCH_UNKNOWN.
adjacentFindings.disposition: Separate architect ruling when root schedules it. Either the runner maps it to an existing in-set reason, or the reviewed set is amended with security review. The R8.2 logging will make it observable.

adjacentFindings.what: Runner seam tests use fake backends that return 200 to any FINAL. That is how this mismatch shipped. The R8.3 predicate-applying fake closes it for this seam only.

security: No broadening of the ADMITTED->FINALIZING pre-Ready edge. The runner still cannot obtain API CANCELLED or AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED without the backend's own record.
No invented cause: a control loss is reported as unmapped ERROR, as AC-13 requires.

The new logs are fixed templates with server-owned ids and constants. They never contain report content, errorMessage or the response message, so there is no log injection and no secret or canary path. The canary test enforces this.
Fail-closed is kept: the self-stop still stops the run before any step. Only its terminal label changes, from a false 'cancelled' to the truthful 'run fault: cancelled'.
